question: What is the main job of wearable health devices in clinical care?

options.A: To deliver oral medications automatically to the patient
options.B: To diagnose complex surgical diseases without a doctor
options.C: To track and transmit health-related data continuously
options.D: To replace traditional laboratory blood testing completely

explanation: Wearables are great because they keep an eye on patient vitals between clinic visits. You've got this!

question: Which wearable device is best for continuous, medical-grade heart rhythm monitoring?
explanation: Medical patches stick securely and are specifically designed to catch every beat of critical heart rhythms accurately.

question: How do optical sensors in regular fitness wristbands usually measure your heart rate?

options.A: By measuring electrical currents through the skin
options.B: By detecting changes in blood flow using light
options.C: By listening to heart valve closures via tiny microphones
options.D: By calculating body temperature shifts on the wrist

explanation: Think of how a flashlight shines through your fingers—these sensors use light to catch the pulse of blood moving underneath your skin!

question: What fluid do continuous glucose monitors sample to check a patient's sugar levels?
explanation: The tiny sensor sits right under the skin, swimming in the fluid surrounding your cells (interstitial fluid) to estimate blood sugar.

question: Why is tracking data over time with a wearable better than a single blood pressure check at the clinic?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to manually record any vital signs
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will take all prescribed medications
options.D: It captures daily trends and avoids single-visit anxiety spikes

explanation: Ever get nervous seeing a doctor in a white coat? Wearables show real everyday trends without hospital stress getting in the way.

question: A heart failure patient uses a wearable at home. Which trend should make a nurse step in early?

options.A: Gradual upward trends in daily weight and decreasing physical activity
options.B: Stable resting heart rates recorded consistently throughout the night
options.C: Occasional reminders to stand up and stretch during sedentary hours
options.D: A slight increase in daily step counts reported over the weekend

explanation: When activity drops and weight creeps up from fluid, it's often an early warning sign that heart failure symptoms are worsening.

question: What is an important nursing duty when giving a wearable device to a patient?

options.A: Writing custom software code to link the device to the hospital
options.B: Calibrating the internal microchips using a sterile surgical kit
options.C: Teaching the patient how to wear, charge, and sync the device
options.D: Replacing the device hardware components whenever the battery dies

explanation: As a nurse, your guidance is key! Patients need to know how to handle, charge, and sync their devices so the data keeps flowing.

question: Why do nurses set specific alert limits (thresholds) on patient wearables?

options.A: To ensure the device battery never runs out of power unexpectedly
options.B: To stop patients from looking at their own heart rate data
options.C: To comply with government laws regarding smartphone manufacturing
options.D: To prevent alert fatigue from minor, harmless data fluctuations

explanation: Setting smart limits stops alarms from ringing over tiny movements, keeping nurses focused on actual emergencies.

question: Why is data encryption so important for health wearable devices?

options.A: To increase the physical durability of the wristband strap
options.B: To protect sensitive patient health records from unauthorized interception
options.C: To ensure the step counter measures distance more accurately
options.D: To make the device battery last much longer during daily use

explanation: Encryption scrambles personal health details so hackers can't read or steal confidential patient information.

question: Which of these is NOT an ethical concern when using health wearables?

options.A: Ensuring equal access for patients regardless of income
options.B: Obtaining proper informed consent for data sharing
options.C: Protecting personal health information from data breaches
options.D: Increasing the physical battery weight of the wristband

explanation: Battery weight is just hardware design, while privacy, consent, and equal access are major ethical issues in nursing informatics.

question: What is a major challenge when using wearable health devices in some Nigerian communities?

options.A: Excessive availability of high-speed fiber optic cables
options.B: Strict government bans on all digital wristwatches
options.C: A complete lack of patients suffering from chronic illnesses
options.D: Unstable electricity supply and limited internet connectivity

explanation: Frequent power cuts and poor network signals can sometimes make it tough to keep live health data syncing smoothly.

question: How can healthcare providers help patients who struggle with technology when using wearables?

options.A: By refusing care to anyone who does not understand technology immediately
options.B: By removing all digital screens from the monitoring equipment
options.C: By forcing all patients to buy the most expensive smartphone available
options.D: By providing simple, guided education and easy-to-use device interfaces

explanation: Patience and clear, step-by-step teaching help bridge the digital gap so every patient feels comfortable using their tracker.
